chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kallub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Ja'far, from his father, that 'Ali عليه السلام used to say:
“In ghusl (ritual bath) from janabah and in wudu (ablution), of it there suffices that amount which suffices of oil, that which moistens the body.”

key_terms.الدُّهْنِ: oil; used here as a comparison for light but complete covering
key_terms.الْجَسَدَ: the body; the area to be reached by moisture in this wording
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: major ritual impurity caused by janabah
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution); the ritual washing for prayer
key_terms.اَلْغُسْلُ: ritual bath; the full washing required in a state of major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: How much water is sufficient for ghusl (ritual bath) from janabah and for wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the minimum extent of water application in ghusl (ritual bath) for janabah and wudu (ablution). It indicates that what is required is an amount sufficient to moisten and cover the body, expressed through the comparison to oil that reaches and moistens the skin.
